### Problem: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable {#sec-pref-p4-a}

::: {.p-statement}
A fixed matrix of size $m \times n$ ($1 \le m, n \le 200$, $-10^4 \le$ cell $\le 10^4$) and up to $10^4$ calls to `sumRegion(row1, col1, row2, col2)`, each returning the sum of the sub-matrix with those **inclusive, 0-based** corners.

Source: [LC 304 · Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable](https://leetcode.com/problems/range-sum-query-2d-immutable/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Every rectangle is "big anchored block minus two anchored blocks plus the overlap". Build the block table once and the rectangle costs four reads — the sign pattern is exactly the inclusion–exclusion of @sec-pref-2d.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Brute force.** Loop the query rectangle: $O(mn)$ per call, $10^4 \cdot 4\cdot10^4 = 4\cdot10^{8}$ in the worst case.
2. **2D prefix table.** Build $P$ of size $(m+1)\times(n+1)$ in $O(mn)$. For an inclusive query, the half-open rectangle is $[r_1, r_2{+}1) \times [c_1, c_2{+}1)$, so read $P[r_2{+}1][c_2{+}1] - P[r_1][c_2{+}1] - P[r_2{+}1][c_1] + P[r_1][c_1]$.
3. The `+1` padding is what makes row $0$ and column $0$ legal reads: a query touching the top-left corner needs no branch.

**Invariant.** $P[i][j] = \sum_{r<i, c<j} a[r][c]$, which the stress test below checks against a double loop for every random rectangle.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Walk the rectangle

::: {.form-next}
A query names two corners, so loop the rows between them and the columns between those: $O(mn)$ per call, and $10^4$ calls on a $200 \times 200$ matrix is $4\cdot10^8$ additions. Each answer is computed once and then thrown away, even though neighbouring rectangles overlap almost entirely.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def sum_region_brute(mat, r1, c1, r2, c2):
    return sum(mat[i][j] for i in range(r1, r2 + 1) for j in range(c1, c2 + 1))
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int sumRegionBrute(const vector<vector<int>>& a,
                   int r1, int c1, int r2, int c2) {
    int tot = 0;
    for (int i = r1; i <= r2; ++i)
        for (int j = c1; j <= c2; ++j) tot += a[i][j];
    return tot;
}
```
:::

#### Four reads

::: {.form-next}
The rectangle is what is left of the bottom-right anchored block after the two strips above and to the left are removed — and removing their overlap once too often is fixed by adding it back. Build the anchored-block table $P$ once, and a query becomes $P[r_2{+}1][c_2{+}1] - P[r_1][c_2{+}1] - P[r_2{+}1][c_1] + P[r_1][c_1]$: four reads whatever the rectangle's size. The `+1` padding is what makes row $0$ and column $0$ legal reads, so a query touching the top-left corner needs no branch.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]

    assert str(final) == "[8, 11, 12]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arr-range-sum-2d
class NumMatrix:
    def __init__(self, matrix):
        self.p = build_prefix2d(matrix)

    def sumRegion(self, r1: int, c1: int, r2: int, c2: int) -> int:   # inclusive
        p = self.p
        return p[r2 + 1][c2 + 1] - p[r1][c2 + 1] - p[r2 + 1][c1] + p[r1][c1]


for _ in range(200):
    m = random.randint(1, 7)
    n = random.randint(1, 7)
    mat = [[random.randint(-9, 9) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(m)]
    nm = NumMatrix(mat)
    for _ in range(15):
        r1 = random.randint(0, m - 1)
        c1 = random.randint(0, n - 1)
        r2, c2 = random.randint(r1, m - 1), random.randint(c1, n - 1)
        assert nm.sumRegion(r1, c1, r2, c2) == sum_region_brute(mat, r1, c1, r2, c2)

official = [[3, 0, 1, 4, 2], [5, 6, 3, 2, 1], [1, 2, 0, 1, 5], [4, 1, 0, 1, 7], [1, 0, 3, 0, 5]]
nm = NumMatrix(official)
assert nm.sumRegion(2, 1, 4, 3) == 8
assert nm.sumRegion(1, 1, 2, 2) == 11
assert nm.sumRegion(1, 2, 2, 4) == 12
assert nm.sumRegion(0, 0, 4, 4) == sum(sum(r) for r in official)
print("NumMatrix OK")
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

class NumMatrix {
    vector<vector<int>> p;
public:
    NumMatrix(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size(), n = matrix[0].size();
        p.assign(m + 1, vector<int>(n + 1, 0));
        for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
            int rowsum = 0;
            for (int j = 0; j < n; ++j) {
                rowsum += matrix[i][j];
                p[i + 1][j + 1] = p[i][j + 1] + rowsum;     // eq-pref-2d-build
            }
        }
    }
    int sumRegion(int r1, int c1, int r2, int c2) {         // inclusive
        return p[r2 + 1][c2 + 1] - p[r1][c2 + 1]
             - p[r2 + 1][c1]     + p[r1][c1];              // eq-pref-2d-query
    }
};
```
:::
:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Walk the rectangle** is $O(mn)$ per query and $O(1)$ space: $4\cdot10^8$ additions for $10^4$ queries on a $200 \times 200$ matrix. **Four reads** is $O(mn)$ once to build and then $O(1)$ per query, for $O(mn + q)$ overall. **Space** $O(mn)$ — here $201^2$ integers, nothing to apologise for. Values are signed, so the table can be negative; that changes nothing about the construction, but it does kill any "binary search on the answer" shortcut in @sec-pref-p4-b.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- A single-cell query: the four reads collapse to $a[r][c]$.
- A query reaching row $0$ or column $0$: reads a cell of row $0$ or column $0$ of $P$, which are the padding zeros.
- A $1\times1$ matrix and a full-matrix query: both are the same code path — the padding is why.
- Empty input rows would break `matrix[0].size()` in C++; the constraints guarantee $m, n \ge 1$, so translate the guard once if your judge allows $0$.
:::
